info.name: Doriath API Contract Suite
info.description:
Newman/Postman API-contract tests for the Doriath (vault) Nextcloud app. Locks the HTTP contract of doriath's controllers (appinfo/routes.php + lib/Controller/*): secrets, encryption suites, CA status, folders, secret-types, and the public link-share access endpoint. Every family is exercised for a happy path, an error/validation case (4xx, not 500 where the controller is correct), and an authorization case (no auth -> 401, or 404 for the public token route). The suite is self-contained and idempotent: it creates the vault objects it needs (a secret, a folder) and deletes them again in teardown.

This suite asserts the Phase-0 fixes: secret create returns 201 with ownerType:"user" (not 500); secret/suite/folder reads return their list/object shape; the public link-share token route is reachable without NC auth and 404s on an unknown token.

Most vault WRITES that mint or use key material (suite create, private-key upload, link-share create) require the in-browser RSA crypto flow and an unlocked vault with a freshly-generated key — they are not drivable from a headless API client and are QUARANTINED honestly below (covered by Playwright). What IS drivable from the API — because the dev vault already has an unlocked suite — is the full secret CRUD round-trip, folder create, and all the reads + authz, which this suite exercises.

AUTH MODEL: collection auth is noauth; every authenticated request carries an EXPLICIT basic-auth block (admin:admin via adminUser/adminPass). The no-auth requests target {{noAuthBase}} (127.0.0.1) so the host-scoped NC session cookie established on {{baseUrl}} (localhost) is never sent to them. Run with --ignore-redirects. See run-newman.sh.

GAP-4 FIX (previously quarantined): SecretController::create and EncryptionSuiteController::create now declare their required params nullable and validate presence in the body, so OMITTING a required field returns a clean JSON 400 instead of NC's reflection param-injection 500 HTML page. EncryptionSuiteController::create additionally catches InvalidArgumentException from the key-signing path, so an invalid public key also degrades to a 400. The corresponding create-error tests now assert 400 (not the old quarantined 500).
